headline: Reuters Oct 24 reports a US-official campaign to restore the Bolsonaro clan
dek: Brazil votes today, Oct 25, in the presidential runoff between incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva (80) and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro (45). First round Oct 4: Flavio 47.03% of valid votes, Lula 45.16% (TSE count) — a 1.87-point gap; neither cleared 50%.
sources: Brazil Superior Electoral Court (TSE) election calendar via Sunday Guardian; Reuters Oct 24 investigation (10 current/former US officials); Al Jazeera Oct 23 preview; CNN Oct 25; The Hindu Oct 24 (final debate); Turkiye
fault_line: Should Brazil align with Trump's US or hold its leftist sovereignty line — is this vote a referendum on Lula's legacy or on the Bolsonaro family's return?

sections.what_happened: Brazil votes today, Oct 25, in the presidential runoff between incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva (80) and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro (45). First round Oct 4: Flavio 47.03% of valid votes, Lula 45.16% (TSE count) — a 1.87-point gap; neither cleared 50%. Final polls disagree: CNT/MDA (Oct 21-23, n=2,032) puts Flavio ahead (46.3% vs 45% voting intentions; 50.7% vs 49.3% valid votes per one readout), while Datafolha Oct 22 showed a 50-50 tie — outcome genuinely uncertain. 158.7m electors eligible; polls 08:00-17:00 Brasilia (20:00 UTC = 00:00 Oct 26); results expected within hours of close. Reuters Oct 24: two US State Department officials (Darren Beattie, senior adviser for Western Hemisphere affairs, and Ricardo Pita, deputy assistant secretary for North America) led a campaign to restore the Bolsonaro clan, pushing sanctions aimed at tilting the election; after Jair Bolsonaro's 27-year sentence (Sept 2025) they pivoted to his son. Lula has publicly warned Washington against interfering. Inauguration Jan 5, 2027.
sections.what_verified: Reuters (T1) + Al Jazeera (T2, STATE QA) agree on vote-day facts; TSE calendar is the official source of the schedule
sections.what_disputed: Polls conflict (tie vs narrow Flavio lead) — no poll is treated as a forecast. Reuters' campaign account rests on 10 unnamed current/former US officials — attributed, not independently confirmed. One viral social clip mislabels the incumbency (calling Bolsonaro the incumbent); the record follows TSE/Reuters/CNN: Lula is the incumbent.
sections.why_matters: The election Washington tried to tilt: Brazil votes today with the US campaign to restore the Bolsonaros now on the record — and the result lands overnight time.
sections.context: Background: NEW to scans -- Brazil votes today in presidential runoff: Lula vs Flavio Bolsonaro, first-round margin 1.87 points; Reuters Oct 24 reports a US-official campaign to restore the Bolsonaro clan

totw_analysis: Our read: The election Washington tried to tilt: Brazil votes today with the US campaign to restore the Bolsonaros now on the record — and the result lands overnight time. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Should Brazil align with Trump's US or hold its leftist sovereignty line — is this vote a referendum on Lula's legacy or on the Bolsonaro family's return?
